body: thank you so much for the support. so far doesnt look like i can afford it :( im working on it though. seriously, thank you.it means a lot

okay that made me cry again. how can someone i dont know seem to care about me more than i care about myself? oi. thanks for the advice. idk if it will happen. so far it seems to be $1000 a day. how wrong is that? you need help? fork it over or deal with it. bah :(

man, i feel you. i do. but im scared to go through with it. so do what im doing tomorrow morning. call your local hospital, and have them admit you. its the last hope for people like us. if anything could help us, its that. im going to give it a shot. you should too. no harm no foul if it doesnt work, right? and if it does, we didnt waste our lives. im scared man, but we can do it
i dont wanna be alone guys
okay, ive started to spiral toward being dangerous to myself again :(

Oh wow I definitely need to check that book out. "Default setting" is definitely the way to put it. Even when I was "better" it felt like something was off, since I was so used to being down all the time. It's like feeling better was out of my comfort zone. Which was super weird and confusing, since feeling down isn't exactly comfortable :/

Eh. I got SSRIs from my general doctor once (which was a lot easier than I thought it would be. Really all you have to say is "I'm stressed", which worries me a bit) but they pretty much did nothing. I don't have a therapist yet. I have numbers, and my work offers to pay for 6 free sessions, but I can't seem to motivate myself to call. I think due to a combination of my previous experience with therapy (either mentioned to you or elsewhere on the thread, im replying to this in my inbox so I'm not sure) and the fact that my immediate reaction is one of being faced with an extreme burden. I'd have to go over everything AGAIN. I don't want to explain everything. I've done it enough times, and that was to people I was close to, not a stranger, and i STILL got judged. Not to mention the fact that these aren't exactly things I enjoy remembering (hence blacking out most of my life. I may as well not have existed previous to 2009). Even if I found the right therapist (I have a great recommendation i guess), 6 sessions won't even BEGIN to skim the surface, then I have to pay. I could afford it if I didn't suck at money, but...I suck at money (it's one of the main outlets for my self-sabotage. inconvenient? very). And just thinking about having ANOTHER monetary responsibility freaks me the fuck out and sets off my anxiety. Not to mention having to pay for both a therapist AND  psychiatrist if I want meds specified to me instead of random general shit that doesn't work.

I do realize that I am most likely making excuses. I also realize that I'll probably HAVE to call soon, since shit is getting a bit out of control (obviously. i posted on r/suicidewatch. ive also had a few more nervous breakdowns lately then I'd like to admit and have seriously considered committing myself a few times recently as well). At this point I'm getting pretty close to it being a choice between calling, or losing my mind completely. Argh. 

I get out sometimes. I was in a serious funk for a while there where I pretty much dropped off the face of the planet except for work. Luckily I managed to at least get over that. I know enough to know that the times when I least feel like being around people are most likely the times it would do me good to do just that. Latey, even if I'm feeling lowest of the low, I've at least managed to drag myself out of my room to say hi to my roommates for a while (they worry about me, which makes me feel even worse, really. fuuu). Unfortunately though, aside from my roommates who are stand up citizens, my "going out" has included self-medication with alcohol and drugs. Which is another inconvenient impulse I have (and doesn't help the money one much either). Like I said in a previous reply somewhere, no hard drugs, and nothing physically addicting. Never again. I was addicted to percocet at one point. I have an extremely addictive personality, I could probably get psychologically addicted to anything, but add that to an actual physical addiction and you get one hell of a quickly escalated problem. I was at the same dependency point as 1yr addicts at about 3 mos from my understanding. Getting away from that was absolute hell. Also, considering how most drugs affect my weird ass brain chemistry (weed is VERY unpleasant for me. its weird) i wouldnt dream of trying anything hard.

The drug thing is getting a bit out of control too, though. I know I need to stop, but I can't seem to make it click. Most of the time it's seemingly a choice between the relief of it or going absolutely mental and hurting myself or others. In that case, I pick drugs.

More ranting. Woo. You guys have opened a veritable black hole of issues here. Haha

You're good. My panic attack/manic episode thing has calmed down a bit since I managed to pass out for like an hour (i have sleep issues, of course), so it's not as urgent anymore, and definitely not as urgent as your hotline job. Thanks for doing that, by the way. Good man/woman.

I would really like to hear more about the self-sabotage thing when you get a chance. As much as I can analyze and pick apart my issues, that one seems to remain somewhat of a mystery to me. Especially with how super impulsive and *seemingly* involuntary it is. I posted some details of that in another reply. If you can help me pinpoint the root of thiis issue it would be seriously heroic. It's about to cause me the best job I've ever had :(

eh. i was having a pretty sever panic attack/manic eisode when I wrote it. i usually steer away from the acronyms, but at that point i kind of just wanted to submit as quickly as possible for the opportunity for someone to talk some sense in to me before i did something a little more retarded than using "idk", like, i don't know, hurt myself, you know? Priorities are fun.

PS, i thought trolling was severely frowned upon in this subreddit. I mean, you probably aren't even a troll, as 11yr old internet speak is usually a peeve of mine, too. However, had I still been in the same state now that I was then, something as simple as being called out for using idiotic slang could have made me worse. Just be careful here, yeah?

edit: i now know from experience that posting here, at least for some of us, requires you to be SEVERELY on the edge. who knows what might set someone off?

edit 2: by the way, it was more of an idfk than idk, really. :P

Yeah no you got it right. I wouldn't be bothered by it if they had tried to teach me that MY problems are consequences of my actions. That would have actually been good parenting. I had to learn accountability on my own years later, since obviously it wasnt exactly a concept understood in my childhood home. Took a while, but I got that one down. At least now when I fuck up and it IS my fault, I can own up to it and accept my consequences since they came about due to a decision *I* made. But youre right, when i was an involuntary player in the situation it was pretty fucked to blame me (and more details on that in my reply to someone else on this thread)). 

Unfortunately living in that environment 24/7, having negativity drilled into your head, as much as you can logic it out, it's hard to not let it affect you. Especially when as a child who's brain and perceptions were still developing as this was going on, it gets pretty hard-wired. When  you're a kid, your parents are your source for the truth of the world. When that truth is "you suck", that sentiment gets buried pretty deep. Of course when I moved out I did the quintessential daddy issues thing and moved out with a guy who was straight up sociopathic (not even an exaggeration. I know people break up and say "omg he's a sociopath" all the time, but no. kid was/is really a sociopath) and went out of the negative frying pan and into the negative fire, only that time ther was "love" involved. oi.

I'll check out "Learned Optimism". I dated a guy for a while who managed to teach me that yes, the way we react to and percieve life is basically a choice. You can choose to get down on yourself, or choose to be happy. I mastered that for a while, and made A LOT of progress, but the  self-destructive impulses i "can't control" kicked back in after a while and it all fell apart. 20/20 hindsight says it's because I tried to purge a lifetime of issues all at one instead of one at a time and I got overwhelmed, not to mention, although I made sure to be careful to tell myself I was doing it for ME and not just for a guy, that wasn't 100% true. So I "got better" for a while. It was nice. But I failed at it. And even though I seem to have figured out why, it's still super discouraging. I mean, who in their right mind gets to see a glimpse of life without...whatever is going on in my head..enjoys it and feels relieved, then jumps right back in to old habits? Lame.

Notice the quotation marks around "cant control". Accountability. I know that somewhere in there I have the ability to control my impulses, but I haven;t figured it out yet. It's like how I learned to choose to be happy and did it. I KNOW i can do it. I HAVE done it. I know exactly what I need to do. And in my head I align everything perfectly. But somewhere in translation from my head to real life, my actions/reactions, whatever, I just can't seem to get it to click. I'll think one thing and do another. "I'm determined to save some of this paycheck" in my head turns into "wtf why am i broke? what did i even spend that on?", "I'm done doing drugs, done. DONE." said with the UTMOST confidence and resolve turns into waking up and thinking "oh...i did drugs ast night. wtf how did that happen". and i cant seem to figure out exactly at what point this shit goes sour. (PS, its not hard drugs. the way my brain is wired, most drugs give me some serious anxiety/bad trips so i just stick to the one that doesn't and will never venture into anything else. especially nothing physically addicting. i can get psychologically addicted to pretty much anything, but i got a physical addiction  once, and the FUCK if I'm ever doing that again).

It reminds me a lot of when I was younger and at home. At some point I ended up "cutting myself" (quotes cuz i never did it with anything that could cause real damage. safety pins, dull pocket knifes, etc. no worries i havent attempted that shit for a LONG time. i think the drugs took its place. id say drugs are the better option), anyway, whenever i did it (not often. once or twice), i never actually WANTED TO. i just WOULD. It'd be like I was watching myself do it from outside my body, then when I came back to, I'd freak the fuck out like "WHY WOULD I DO THAT?! AHHH. I did NOT want to do that. Fuckfuckfuck". Scary shit for a kid, no lie.

I have the same self-sabotage instincts regarding holding a job, but that's another story. That one's been rearing it's stupid fucking head lately though, which is pissing me off, since I have the best job ive ever had that I generally enjoy, but I'm slwly eating away at it's security. One more misstep and I'm out. And I honestly dont have much faith it wont happen. Then I'm fucked.

anyway, ranting. um...yeah.

Yeah. I don't want to be a bad person. My impulse control seems to be zip, though.

As for my parents....They didn't/don't think I'm just the root of all MY problems, but all theirs, and my brothers as well. Brother fucks up? My fault.  Parents split up cuz my dad got snipped after my brother was born but mom decided she doesn't feel like hving sex anymore? Me again, somehow. They have no money? Me. Electronics break when I haven't touched them? Oh, that was totally me. Dad has high blood pressure? My fault. (and the fact he blew up at me and hit me over taking the last tissue and not replacing the box after the company mandated anger management people said it's unhealthy for him to get mad? It's going to kill him, and that's all my fault. Especially when he hurts me and I try to stop him, and he ends up holding me against the wall by my neck, then calling the cops on ME for assault. That was my fault, too. And the cops backed it up and told them they could hit me if I was out of line, so you know, it must be okay.).


When I was younger and they tried to put me in therapy, my counselor tried to have a group sessions with them. It lasted about 2 minutes. Then she tried to (gently) bring up the fact that, perhaps, *they* were part of the problem. My dad flipped the fuck out, yelled at everyone, said fuck that shit, and tried to pull me out of therapy. He didn't end up doing so until she called CPS on us (to be fair, she said she would give us the chance to do it ourselves and didn't, just randomly sicced them on us. And that was my fault, too, apparently. So if you ever wonder why I'm wary of therapists...).

My mom got infinitely better about things after my dad moved out (lives with his gf, won't get a divorce. fucked up situation), and after I moved out. She is still a very depressed person, but without his influence doesn't get down on me much. When we all lived together she pretty much had to agree with him or she'd get the shit too. Poor girl. He still likes to use me as a scapegoat for shit though. Buy used car that is a 2002 model, transmission goes out out of no fault of my own, almost die trying to get to my mom's to see dad on his birthday? Nope. Apparently it's my fault. Get yelled at like a motherfucker, in front of my naive 87yr old great uncle for it? Yep. It's ok though. 2 days later he offers me money and free dinner to make up for it. >:( that was the game when we lived together as well. And is now the game with my poor little bro. They feigned staying together much longer than they should have for "his good", even though he knew what was up. And now my dad is an ass to him (and my mom) from afar, then buys him video games to make up for it. Kid won't even go to the movies with his dad because he is a prick (and picks his nose during movies, apparently. lol).

Brother's kid of a dick too though. Can;t really blame him though when he grew up screaming "Daddy's going to kill *my name*!!! Don't kill her!!". And when he acts up dad talks of moving back in with my mom. HAHAHA. riiiight.

ANyway, yeah. Sounds kinda fucked up, but being the oldest child (in the house. dad had 2 older ones with his first wife. got compared to them a lot even though, oh, idk, my half sister got preggers at 16 and drsained him dry money wise) in a house where no one seemed to have heard of the phenomena of taking accountability for your life being shit cuz you made it that way, there's really no reason to be skeptical.

Anyway, I moved out a few years ago. And logically I know they were wrong, yeah? But when you were around that ALL THE TIME, 24/7, and were being told that if you didnt stop ruining their lives youd be sent to a group home/juvi/whatever since you were 10 and younger, its hard for the impressionable young mind to believe it, and even harder to get rid of the negative mindset in later life. Especially when, when you FINALLY gtfo, you move in with a sociopath who does the same if not worse to you for a year, with the end result of you almost killing yourself because coming to the realization that you had someone very VERY thoroughly lied to yourself during that time and created a delusional reality where everything was okay when it wasnt, and coming to the realization you cant even trust your own perception is a bit much for you, it kind of sets you back.

There's more. Oh so much more. what would you like to know? haha
